transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dan Roman.
Saudi Arabia says it intercepted a missile
fired at an airport in the capital Riyadh on Sunday,
but another projectile hit a passenger terminal
sparking a fire.
NPR's Aro-Bhatrani reports it comes a day
after 13 people were killed and 300 or more wounded,
some critically, in Houthi attacks at that same airport.
- Saudi Arabia had already suspended flights
and operations at Riyadh airport
when an unknown projectile hit one of its passenger terminals
for the second day in a row.
Yemen's Houthis have struck Saudi airports
four times over the past week,
but Saturday's attacks are the deadliest
on the capital Riyadh in more than a decade.
Among those killed was a U.S. citizen.
The Iran-backed group says its attacks are in response
to more than 2,000 Saudi airstrikes on Houthi areas
in various parts of Yemen in recent weeks.
The group also says it hit an Aramco gas facility
and an oil refinery in Saudi Arabia's eastern province
in the past 24 hours.
Saudi Arabia has not commented on those attacks.
Ayyub Al-Trawi, NPR News, Dubai.
- Several states are dealing with flooding
and high winds in the aftermath of hurricanes
Ayesis and Rachel, NPR's Shondelis Duster reports.
- The remnants of East Ayesis and Rachel
now post-tropical cyclones have caused flooding
across the south and west.
In North Carolina, there were tornado warnings on Sunday
as well as a high risk of flooding from heavy rains.
Rapid river rising is also possible as the system moves out.
A tornado watch is also in effect
for parts of southern Virginia through Sunday night.
The National Weather Service says parts of the southwest,
including southern California,
could receive up to three inches of rain on Sunday.
Forecasters also warned of damaging winds
and life-threatening surf as well as rip currents.
Rain is expected to continue from both East Ayesis
and Rachel through Monday.
Shondelis Duster, NPR News.
- On the Pacific coast of Mexico,
Hurricane Simon is pounding the region
as a category four hurricane.
Election officials around the country
are urging mail-in voters for the midterm elections
to return ballots as soon as possible.
It's because of changes to the mailing system.
NPR's Hansi Lo Wang reports.
- Some post offices now have fewer daily pickups
and a different way of processing mail
to help the U.S. Postal Service
stabilize its shaky finances.
Those changes have raised the risk
of getting your mail-in ballot rejected
if you mail it close to election day.
About a week before November 3rd,
the Postal Service says it plans
to speed up ballot deliveries.
Still, a USPS public service announcement says
if you're voting by mail, do it early.
- We recommend that you mail your completed ballot
before election day and at least a week before the deadline
by which your mail-in ballot must be received
by your local election office.
- Motors with mail-in ballots can also consider
returning them at their local election office
or at any available drop boxes.
Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
- And from Washington, you're listening to NPR News.
Pope Leo will undergo surgery this week
to remove a small growth on his lung.
Megan Williams reports doctors found a nodule
during a routine checkup.
Pope Leo told pilgrims gathered in St. Peter's Square
on Sunday that doctors had found
what he called a localized nodule in his lung.
He said it was detected at a very early stage
and is well-contained, but doctors recommended removing it.
The Vatican says the surgery will take place
in the coming days, with Leo expected to recover
in about a week.
It's the first known health scare for the American Pope
since his election last year.
Leo is physically active and plays tennis regularly.
Next month, he's due to make a 12-day trip
to Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru,
where he lived for two decades and holds citizenship.
The Vatican has not said whether the surgery
will affect those plans.
For NPR News, I'm Megan Williams in Rome.
- The Justice Department is investigating
five television networks that cover the White House
as part of the pool arrangement
for possible antitrust violations.
The five networks, ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC, and Fox,
did not comment on the Justice Department action,
but media and press advocacy groups
are denouncing the latest action.
The move comes just weeks after President Trump removed CNN,
MS, now political, and those three networks
from the White House because he objected
to the way they covered them.
Christina Pike, the Tennessee woman who was unsuccessfully
executed on September 30th, was returned over the weekend
from a hospital to a hospital.
I'm Dan Ronan, NPR.
This message comes from Midi Health.
